metadata.case_name: MANDEEP SINGH v. SOUTHWELL CONSTRUCTION CO. LTD. AND ANOTHER

source: As for the cervical spine, Dr Chiang found mild loss of cervical lordosis
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the neck

injuries.description: posterior extrusion / herniation of L5/S1 disc compressing on the right S1 nerve root causing moderate compression on the right anterior part of the thecal sac
source: The MRI examination taken on 23 April 2005 showed posterior extrusion of L5/S1 disc. The herniated disc was compressed on the right S1 nerve root causing moderate compression of the right anterior part of the thecal sac, which was suspected to be the lesion for the plaintiff’s right lower limb symptoms.
the MRI report showed findings of posterior herniated L5/S1 disc compressing on the right S1 nerve root and causing moderate compression on the right anterior part of the thecal sac;
injuries.icd_description: Injury of nerve root of sacral spine

injuries.description: posterior extrusion / moderate posterior herniation of L4/5 disc
source: Posterior extrusion of L4/5 disc was also seen.
also from the MRI report it showed moderate posterior herniation of the L4/L5 disc caused moderate compression on the anterior part of the thecal sac;
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the abdomen, lower back, lumbar spine or pelvis

injuries.description: slight posterior bulging of L1/2, L2/3 and L3/4 discs; decreased signal intensity in L4/5 and L5/S1 discs indicating disc degeneration and dehydration; minimal lumbar spondylosis
source: There was also slight posterior bulging of L1/2, L2/3, and L3/4 discs which are causing minimal indentation on the anterior part of the thecal sac.
Decreased signal intensity seen in L4/5 and L5/S1 discs indicated disc degeneration and dehydration.
Minimal change of spondylosis was seen in the lumbar spine and no significant degenerative change is seen in the lumbar facet joints.
there were also slight posterior bulging of the L1/2, L2/3 and L3/4 discs and minimal lumbar spondylosis;
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the abdomen, lower back, lumbar spine or pelvis

manifestations.description: pain and tenderness on the right lumbar region
lower lumbar back pain radiating down to the right thigh
able to walk without aid, albeit with a limp
right lower limb symptoms associated with right S1 nerve root compression
reasonable capacity for performing daily activities but required to avoid continuous and prolonged heavy manual work or prolonged stressful posture
permanent impairment assessed to be 10% of the whole person

treatments_received: A&E treatment at Caritas Medical Centre (discharged after treatment)
physiotherapy (attended in March 2004; differing notes as to number of sessions)
follow-ups at Department of Orthopaedics & Traumatology of Caritas Medical Centre
treatments_future: about 40 to 50 sessions of physiotherapy (recommended by Dr Chiang)
surgery unlikely (Dr Chiang stated surgery is unlikely to be required)

losses.description: Permanent impairment assessed to be 10% of the whole person as a result of the plaintiff's lumbar condition.
Walking with a limp; reduced ease of mobility following the accident.
Required to avoid continuous and prolonged heavy manual work and to take up work of a less heavy type than before the accident.
